title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 22 Jun to 2 Sep 2026
summary: From 22 Jun to 2 Sep 2026 the radar shows the lake shrinking from 31.35 km2 to 29.75 km2, or -5.1%. Over the same 72 days HH rose across the land while HV stayed almost the same.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake lost 1.6 km2. Mean HV moved by 0.05 dB, but mean HH rose by 0.56 dB, with 2.45 km2 brighter in HH by more than 3 dB and only 0.23 km2 darker. In HV, 0.61 km2 turned brighter and 0.39 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: Rough dry ground and fields had 1.0 km2 brighter in HH and rose 0.53 dB on average. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes rose 0.56 dB in HH. Built-up land, which should be stable, rose 0.6 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown for irrigation and evaporation; the dam's records would confirm it. Possible cause for the higher HH on every type, built-up land included: a small calibration difference between the two acquisitions; stable targets on more dates would check it. Possible cause on the fields: rougher, drier soil after harvest.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen. Lake areas are approximate: 11.5% and 8.6% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Report the lake loss of 1.6 km2 together with the dam's own level change. Treat the HH rise as uncertain until it is checked against stable targets.
